title: Mastering the Contracted Socket: A Clinical Reconstruction Guide
summary: The contracted socket represents a complex sequela of enucleation or evisceration, characterized by insufficient conjunctival volume and fornix depth. This guide provides a systematic approach to diagnosis, classification, and advanced reconstruction strategies for the reconstructive ocularist and surgeon.

sections.title: Definition & Pathophysiology
sections.content: A contracted socket is a clinical state where the conjunctival sac lacks the necessary volume, surface area, and fornix depth to support a prosthetic eye. Pathophysiology involves myofibroblastic proliferation, chronic inflammation, and fibrosis of the subconjunctival connective tissue, leading to scar contracture and loss of the inferior/superior fornices.

rows: Severe: Significant contracture, no fornix depth
Total: Obliteration of the conjunctival sac

sections.title: Clinical Examination Checklist
content: Assessment of superior and inferior fornix depth.
Evaluation of eyelid margin position (entropion/ectropion).
Assessment of orbital implant volume (implant exposure/migration).
Examination of conjunctival mucosa for keratinization or symblepharon.
Palpation of the orbit for orbital floor fractures or implant mobility.
Measurement of the 'prosthetic eye retention' capacity.

sections.title: Red Flags: Immediate Referral
content: Exposed hydroxyapatite or porous polyethylene implant.
Socket pain suggestive of orbital cellulitis.
Rapidly progressive volume loss.
Signs of orbital implant extrusion.
Severe pyogenic granuloma formation.

sections.title: Management Algorithm
content: Step 1: Treat underlying inflammation (Topical antibiotics/steroids).
Step 2: Conservative management (Prosthetic resizing/expansion).
Step 3: Mild cases: Fornix reconstruction with mucosal grafting.
Step 4: Severe cases: Dermis-fat graft or orbital implant exchange.
Step 5: Total obliteration: Ocular surface reconstruction/orbital prosthesis.

sections.title: Surgical Techniques: Key Pearls
content: Mucosal Grafting: Buccal mucosa is the gold standard for donor tissue.
Dermis-Fat Graft: Excellent for secondary implant volume correction.
Tissue Expanders: Used in severely scarred, contracted sockets prior to reconstruction.
Symblepharon Lysis: Release of cicatricial bands with spacer placement.
Anterior Orbitotomy: Necessary for complete implant exchange or removal.

content.explanation: V: Vertical fornix depth, O: Orbital implant position, L: Lid margin stability, U: Underlying cicatrization, M: Mucosa integrity, E: External orbital bony support.

sections.title: Recent Advances
sections.content: Recent studies suggest the use of amniotic membrane transplantation (AMT) in conjunction with mitomycin-C to inhibit fibroblastic activity and recurrence. Advanced 3D-printed patient-specific orbital implants are currently under clinical investigation to restore superior socket volume.
